observation_summary: The method `BaseSingleFieldPeriod.between` throws an `IllegalFieldValueException` when calculating the difference between `MonthDay` objects involving February 29th, because it attempts to set the date on a base year (1970) that does not support leap days.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the base reference time used for the calculation from 0L (1970-01-01) to a leap year (1972-01-01). This is a correction to the computational strategy (the algorithm) used to calculate the difference between partial dates, ensuring that leap days are valid within the calculation context. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a simple variable initialization (Assignment), but a change to the procedural logic of the calculation.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows the error occurs during `chrono.set(start, 0L)` where 0L represents the epoch (1970), which is not a leap year.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the introduction of `START_1972` and its use in `chrono.set(start, START_1972)` instead of `0L`.
The bug report confirms that the issue is the inability to handle February 29th when using the default epoch.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a constant was introduced, the primary issue is the algorithmic approach of using a non-leap year as the base for date calculations involving potential leap days.
The fix does not add a guard or validation check; it changes the underlying data used for the calculation to avoid the invalid state entirely.
